criteria.text: The allergen(s) to which the patient is allergic must be clinically relevant.
criteria.source_quote: The allergen(s) to which the patient is allergic must be clinically relevant
criteria.if_missing: Is the allergen identified as clinically relevant to the patient's history and exposure?

criteria.text: Trial of avoidance measures has failed or there is unavoidable exposure to allergy triggers identified in allergy testing.
criteria.source_quote: Trial of avoidance measures has failed or there is unavoidable exposure to allergy triggers identified in allergy testing
criteria.if_missing: Did avoidance measures fail, or is there documentation of unavoidable exposure to the identified trigger?
criteria.short: No documented avoidance failure or unavoidable exposure

criteria.text: The patient's condition must be one of the covered indications (allergic rhinitis, allergic conjunctivitis, allergic asthma, dust mite atopic dermatitis, or stinging insect hypersensitivity).
criteria.source_quote: Conditions for which immunotherapy will be considered medically reasonable and necessary include
criteria.if_missing: What is the patient's diagnosis for which immunotherapy is being requested?

criteria.text: Immunotherapy for food hypersensitivity is not covered.
criteria.if_missing: Is the immunotherapy being given for food hypersensitivity?

criteria.text: Immunotherapy for cockroach hypersensitivity is not covered.
criteria.if_missing: Is the immunotherapy being given for cockroach hypersensitivity?

criteria.text: Immunotherapy for urticaria and/or angioedema is not covered.
criteria.if_missing: Is the immunotherapy being given for urticaria or angioedema?
Is the requested therapy a provocation-neutralization therapy?

criteria.text: Low-dose subcutaneous therapy based on the Rinkel method is not covered.
criteria.source_quote: Low-dose subcutaneous therapy based on the Rinkel method
criteria.if_missing: Is the requested therapy low-dose subcutaneous therapy based on the Rinkel method?

criteria.text: Therapy formulations such as allergoids or adjuvants are not covered.
criteria.source_quote: Therapy formulations, such as allergoids or adjuvants
criteria.if_missing: Does the therapy use allergoid or adjuvant formulations?

criteria.text: Oral/sublingual for food, epicutaneous, intralymphatic, intranasal, or sublingual routes of administration are not covered.
criteria.if_missing: What is the route of administration for the immunotherapy?

criteria.text: Immunotherapy for Hymenoptera venom sensitivity using whole-body extracts (except fire ant extracts) is not covered.
criteria.source_quote: Immunotherapy for Hymenoptera venom sensitivity using whole-body extracts, with the exception of fire ant extracts
criteria.if_missing: Is whole-body extract (other than fire ant) being used for Hymenoptera venom immunotherapy?

criteria.text: Patients should not have substantial comorbid conditions that could increase immunotherapy risk.
criteria.source_quote: Patients should not have substantial comorbid conditions that could increase immunotherapy risk
criteria.if_missing: Does the patient have substantial comorbid conditions (e.g., severe uncontrolled asthma, significant cardiovascular disease) that increase immunotherapy risk?

criteria.text: Patients on beta-blockers and/or ACE inhibitors must have an individualized risk versus benefit assessment prior to receiving inhalant or venom allergen immunotherapy.
criteria.source_quote: Patients on beta-blockers and/or angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor medications must have individualized assessments of risk versus benefit prior to receiving inhalant or venom allergen immunotherapy
criteria.if_missing: If the patient is on a beta-blocker or ACE inhibitor, was an individualized risk vs benefit assessment documented prior to immunotherapy?
criteria.short: No individualized risk/benefit assessment for beta-blocker/ACE inhibitor patient

criteria.text: Patients should be able to cooperate during therapy.
criteria.source_quote: Patients should be able to cooperate during therapy
criteria.if_missing: Is the patient able to cooperate during immunotherapy administration?
criteria.short: Patient unable to cooperate during therapy

not_modeled.quote: A presumption of failure can be made when, after 12-24 months of therapy, a person does not experience: A noticeable decrease of symptoms, An increase in tolerance to the offending allergen, and A reduction in medication usage.
not_modeled.why: This is a clinical response/monitoring guideline for continuation decisions, not a discrete pre-authorization eligibility criterion checkable from a single fact; it's a compound judgment about treatment response over time.

not_modeled.quote: For many patients, the recommended duration of allergen immunotherapy is 3-5 years.
not_modeled.why: A general duration recommendation, not a strict coverage requirement; described as individualized, not testable as pass/fail.

not_modeled.quote: Home administration of allergen immunotherapy should only be considered in rare and exceptional cases when the benefits of immunotherapy clearly outweigh the risks.
not_modeled.why: Subjective judgment about rare/exceptional cases without a clear testable fact; site-of-service rule is discretionary and narrative rather than a bright-line criterion.

not_modeled.quote: Services will be considered medically reasonable and necessary when all aspects of care are within the scope of practice of the provider's professional licensure
not_modeled.why: Provider licensure/scope-of-practice compliance depends on state law specifics not captured in a simple fact vocabulary for this packet-level tool.
